title: Entity structure decision: LLC, S-corp, or C-corp
summary: The entity decision shapes taxes, liability, retirement plan options, and exit pathways for years.
detailsHtml:
The three primary options for U.S. operating businesses

LLC taxed as a partnership or sole proprietor: Simplest. All profits flow through to personal returns, all subject to SE tax. Best for early-stage businesses, businesses with significant reinvestment that exceeds owner draws, or businesses with passive members.

S-corp (or LLC electing S-corp status): Profits flow through, but a "reasonable salary" portion is W-2 (subject to payroll tax) and the rest is distributions (not subject to payroll tax). Saves SE tax once net income exceeds ~$50–80K. Limits to 100 shareholders (family members within 6 generations from a common ancestor count as one shareholder under IRC §1361(c)(1)), all US persons or eligible trusts (ESBTs and QSSTs permitted with elections), single class of stock — constrains outside investment.

C-corp: Separate taxpayer. 21% federal corporate rate. Double-taxation on dividends, but unlimited retained earnings at the corporate rate. Required for venture funding (VCs need preferred stock). Section 1202 Qualified Small Business Stock can exclude up to $10M of gain on sale if held >5 years — a powerful tool for founders.

Tax comparison at $500K business profit, owner takes all: LLC sole prop: SE tax + ordinary income → ~40-45% effective S-corp: $150K salary + $350K distribution → ~33-38% effective C-corp: $105K corp tax + $300K dividends taxed twice → ~38-42% C-corp + retained earnings: 21% on retained portion → potentially lowest but locked at corporate level until distribution

The conversion question

Most businesses start as LLCs (simple, flexible) and elect S-corp once profits warrant. Conversion to C-corp is irreversible for five years after election (can revoke S-corp but cannot re-elect for 5 years). Get this advice from a CPA who specializes in your business stage; the wrong election can cost six figures over a decade.
